newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes to boost production of SLK car.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes to boost production of SLK car.

text.p: German automaker Mercedes-Benz AG said on Thursday it will boost production of its popular SLK roadster by about 30 percent and create 500 new jobs in the next two years due to strong demand.

Instead of the planned production of 35,000 vehicles, Mercedes will build about 42,000 of the new cars in 1997 and about 46,000 in 1998 at its plant in Bremen, Mercedes board member Manfred Remel told a news conference.
Remel said higher production will be accomplished through an increase in the operating hours at the plant, to 21 hours per day from 18 hours, and a return to three shifts from two shifts.
Mercedes said it would invest 25 million marks ($16.6 million) into the additional production capacity. In addition, 500 jobs would be added at the plant, raising employment to 14,000.
The new employees will come from training programmes within Mercedes and also from other units of parent company Daimler-Benz AG, where layoffs are taking place.

Mercedes downplayed published reports that it may stop advertising for the vehicle, which has been sold out through 1998. But Remel said Mercedes has reviewed its planning for the car and has cancelled some of its campaigns.

The SLK was introduced in September 1995 at a price of about 53,000 marks ($35,000). Company officials said in July that two-thirds of the SLKs ordered by that point had been to customers who had not previously owned a Mercedes.
